name: asub
title: Arbitrary subsetting of array-like objects at specified indices

origin.description: Subset array-like objects at specified indices. asub() is a S3 generic, with one method, asub.default, supplied in the abind package.
origin.usage: asub(x, idx, dims = seq(length.out = max(length(dim(x)), 1)), drop = NULL, ...)

arguments.name: idx
arguments.text: A list of indices (e.g., a list of a mixture of integer, character, and logical vectors, but can actually be anything). Can be just a vector in the case that length(dims)==1. NULL entries in the list will be treated as empty indices.

arguments.name: dims
arguments.text: The dimensions on which to index (a numeric or integer vector). The default is all of the dimensions.

arguments.name: drop
arguments.text: The drop argument to index with (the default is to not supply a drop argument).
There are no additional arguments allowed for asub.default but other methods may use them.

origin.details: Constructs and evaluates an expression to do the requested indexing. E.g., for x with length(dim(x))==4 the call asub(x, list(c("a","b"), 3:5), 2:3) will construct and evaluate the expression x[, c("a","b"), 3:5, ], and the call asub(x, 1, 2, drop=FALSE) will construct and evaluate the expression x[, 1, , , drop=FALSE]. asub checks that the elements of dims are in the range 1 to length(dim(x)) (in the case that x is a vector, length(x) is used for dim(x)). Other than that, no checks are made on the suitability of components of idx as indices for x.
origin.value: A subset of x, as returned by x[...].
origin.example:
x <- array(1:24,dim=c(2,3,4),dimnames=list(letters[1:2],LETTERS[1:3],letters[23:26]))
print(asub(x, 1, 1, drop=FALSE))
print(asub(x, list(1:2,3:4), c(1,3)))

translation.description: Subset array-like objects at specified indices. This follows asub.default from abind.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: The object to index, as a NumPy array or abind Array.

arguments.name: idx
arguments.text: Indices for the dimensions in dims. Use a list when len(dims) > 1; a vector is accepted when only one dimension is indexed. None entries in a list mean an empty index on that dimension.

arguments.name: dims
arguments.text: 1-based dimension numbers to index. The default is every dimension of x.

arguments.name: drop
arguments.text: When False, keep length-1 dimensions like R's drop=FALSE. When None, R's default drop applies and all singleton dimensions are removed.

arguments.name: **kwargs
arguments.text: Not allowed for this method; extra keywords raise an error.

translation.details: Builds R-style combined indexing on column-major data. Character indices use dimnames on an Array. With drop=None, singleton dimensions are dropped after indexing, matching R's default [ behavior.
translation.value: A subset of x with the same type as the input when x is an Array; otherwise a NumPy array.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from abind.abind import Array
from abind.asub import asub

x = Array(
    np.arange(1, 25).reshape((2, 3, 4), order="F"),
    dimnames=[list("ab"), list("ABC"), list("wxyz")],
)
print(asub(x, 1, 1, drop=False))
print(asub(x, [np.array([1, 2]), np.array([3, 4])], dims=[1, 3]))
